rationale: The available literature demonstrates that seizures are a core but variable feature of biallelic GTF3C3-related neurodevelopmental disorder (OMIM #621201). Direct phenotypic characterization in small cohorts such as Abdel-Hamid et al. (2025) identified clinical seizures in exactly 2 of 4 (50%) individuals, while zebrafish gtf3c3 knockout models also exhibited seizure susceptibility. Broader systematic and curated disease descriptions (e.g., López 2026, ESHG 2023, PanelApp, OMIM) consistently classify epilepsy/seizures as a defining cardinal feature of the syndrome, yielding pooled historical frequencies around 80%. No literature source refutes the occurrence or phenotypic variability of seizures across cohorts.

evidence.text: In a study characterizing biallelic variants in GTF3C3 across four individuals from three unrelated families, seizures were documented in exactly half (2/4, 50%) of the patients. Functional knockout in zebrafish confirmed increased seizure susceptibility.

source.title: Biallelic variants in GTF3C3 encoding a subunit of the TFIIIC2 complex are associated with neurodevelopmental phenotypes in humans and zebrafish
source.quote: Seizures were observed in half of the patients. Exome/genome sequencing revealed four different GTF3C3 variants including three missense (p.Cys172Gly, p.Val427Phe and p.Ala509Thr) and one nonsense variant (p.Arg717Ter)... Knockout of the GTF3C3 ortholog in zebrafish recapitulated the key clinical symptoms including microcephaly, brain anomalies and seizure susceptibility.

evidence.text: Characterization of novel biallelic GTF3C3 variants and comprehensive review supports the inclusion of GTF3C3 in syndromic neurodevelopmental disorder differential diagnosis, specifically highlighting presentation with CNS malformations and seizures.

new_directions.question_text: What specific electroclinical seizure types and EEG patterns (e.g., hypsarrhythmia, focal spikes, generalized spike-wave) predominate in GTF3C3-related disorder, and does age at onset correlate with variant severity?
new_directions.rationale: The exact seizure semiology across patient cohorts remains under-characterized in primary summaries; determining electroclinical features is essential to distinguish GTF3C3-related epilepsy from other POLR3/TFIIIC-associated neurodevelopmental syndromes.

new_directions.question_text: Does the presence of structural hindbrain malformations (predominant cerebellar atrophy and hypoplasia) predict pharmacoresistance or earlier seizure onset in GTF3C3 patients?
new_directions.rationale: Cerebellar and frontal hypoplasia are consistently reported in imaging; determining whether these structural CNS anomalies drive or correlate with seizure severity would provide prognostic utility.
